findings.issue: `cargo test --all-features` fails to link the sc-jev-py lib-test binary on macOS (undefined _Py* symbols). The `extension-module` feature enables `pyo3/extension-module`, which deliberately omits libpython linkage, so a test executable cannot link. This is pre-existing and not caused by r-5.
findings.recommendation: Do not use `--all-features` for test runs on sc-jev-py. Either run `cargo test` with default features, or exclude the crate (`cargo test --workspace --all-features --exclude sc-jev-py`). Alternatively, gate `pyo3/extension-module` behind a maturin-only build, or document the exclusion in CI. Clippy with --all-features passes, so only test linking is affected.
findings.evidence: The same link error (`Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: _PyBool_Type, _PyBytes_AsString, ...`) reproduces on baseline 77fffdb in a detached worktree with `cargo test --all-features -p sc-jev-py --lib`. `git diff --stat 77fffdb..HEAD` shows no changes under crates/sc-jev-py or any Cargo.toml. Default-feature `cargo test` passes.

notes: Answer to the developer's question: the sc-jev-py link failure is pre-existing. It comes from the pyo3 `extension-module` feature, not from r-5. It reproduces on baseline 77fffdb.
fmt, clippy (all-targets, all-features, -D warnings), and default `cargo test` all pass on 14f85f1. No test failures were observed.

The r-5 diff touches sc-jev, sc-jev-backends, sc-jev-check, docs, and the decision-schema fixtures. I reviewed it through execution facts only and made no structural review. A rust-best-practices review may be warranted for the large crates/sc-jev/src/check.rs rewrite.
The link warnings about ring being built for macOS 15.4 and linked at 11.0 are noise from the deployment target and are not blocking.
